title: fix: consolidate community monitor reliability and safety
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Moves the community monitor to systemd-supervised fresh processes and keeps its committed prompt/runtime files synchronized from `main`.
- Adds low-load text and image probes, provider-origin image 4xx classification, bounded billing diagnostics, official-model follow-ups, and daily leaderboard handling.
- Adds a deterministic daily reliability audit: 7-day success below 70% identifies candidates, while current success of at least 80% in the freshest adequately sampled 24h/48h window prevents delayed deactivation after a fix or new fallback.
- Counts successful fallback rescues as successes and requires a fresh provider-failing probe when both recent windows contain fewer than 20 attributable requests.
- Keeps the acute 4-hour incident path separate with its 24-hour grace and limited quota-reset reactivation.

Validation:
- `npx biome check apps/operation/community-monitor/seven-day-health.mjs`
- `node --check apps/operation/community-monitor/seven-day-health.mjs`
- `git diff --check`
- Production-data dry run: 9 current candidates, 4 protected by recent health, 5 low-volume rows requiring a probe; no model state changed.

Supersedes #12372 and #12483. The live EC2 runtime is updated from this branch; automatic repo synchronization remains gated on this PR landing in `main`.

gist.headline: The garden gets a watchdog
gist.blurb: The community monitor now knows the difference between a sick model and one that has already found its footing again. Fresh probes, fallback-aware scoring, and a daily leaderboard keep the hive’s model garden better tended.
gist.summary: Consolidated the community monitor into systemd-supervised fresh processes with synchronized runtime files, low-load text/image probes, fallback-aware success accounting, daily leaderboards, and a deterministic 7-day audit that protects models showing at least 80% success in a recent adequately sampled 24-hour or 48-hour window.
gist.impact: Users get more reliable community model availability because successful fallbacks count as rescues, low-volume provider failures trigger fresh probes, and recently healthy models avoid delayed deactivation after a fix or new fallback.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful garden keeper inspecting a cozy model-health garden: code-plants have small 7-day and 24h/48h status signs, while a CRT monitor robot cheerfully watches fresh text and image probe seedlings. Healthy plants are protected beneath a little glass cloche, fallback vines reconnect a drooping plant to a thriving one, and a tiny daily leaderboard hangs on a garden shed wall.
